newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-DODO HITS FIVE AS SAO PAULO DEMOLISH CRUZEIRO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DODO HITS FIVE AS SAO PAULO DEMOLISH CRUZEIRO.

text.p: Dodo scored all five goals as Sao Paulo crushed Cruzeiro 5-0 away in the Brazilian championship on Wednesday.

Flamengo striker Romario, due to return to Spain's Valencia next week, scored a hat-trick against Goias while Vasco da Gama's Edmundo, sold to Italy's Fiorentina last week, was sent off for the fourth time this year.
Dodo, one of Brazilian soccer's latest revelations, began his rampage by converting a penalty, then scored with a header and a free kick to grab a first-half hat-trick.

The 19-year-old, who was leading scorer in the Sao Paulo championship held in the first half of the year, added two more after the break with another header and a close-range effort following a rebound.
Cruzeiro also missed a penalty as they prepared for next week's Libertadores Cup semifinal with Colo Colo of Chile in the worst possible way.
Romario, who wants to stay in Brazil when his loan from Valencia expires on Sunday, opened with a penalty and also scored with a header and a perfectly executed free-kick in his team's 4-1 away win.
Valencia have indicated they do not want to extend the loan but Flamengo cannot afford to buy back the player they sold last year.
Edmundo, who is to join Fiorentina in December, scored his team's only goal in a 2-1 defeat by Corinthians but was then ordered off for sarcastically applauding the referee after he had been booked.

Defending champions Gremio, who have almost completely dismantled last year's team, slumped to their third defeat in fourt games as they lost 3-0 to Portuguesa, the team they beat in last year's final.
Unrated Parana recorded their fourth straight win as they overcame Bragantino, one of two teams relegated last year but then controversially reinstated.
